requirements_summary: Workload: low-latency chat + embeddings for personalization. Targets: p95 latency <= 120ms for single-region traffic, p99 <= 300ms; sustained throughput 200-250 req/s with bursts to 500 req/s. Reserved infrastructure: minimum 16 A100-equivalent GPUs across primary region with automatic cross-region failover. Data residency: US-only. Ops: 24/7 critical support, 1 hour critical response SLA, access to incident playbooks and audit logs. Maintenance windows: prefer scheduled quarterly windows, 72-hour notice for non-emergency maintenance.
sla_negotiation_notes: Callisto legal submitted redline 2024-11-28: requests 99.99% uptime and 'full ARR' credit for outages > 6 hours — flagged as non-starter

Suggested Redwood position: 99.95% uptime with tiered credits: <99.95% but >=99.5% = 10% monthly credit; <99.5% but >=99.0% = 25% credit; <99.0% = 50% credit up to 3x monthly invoice; negotiate absolute credit cap linked to committed reserved capacity
Maintenance: propose 2 scheduled maintenance windows per quarter (max 4 hours each) with no-credit if announced >=72 hours; emergency fixes excluded but with SLA communication protocol
Support: Redwood proposes 1-hour response for Sev1, 4-hour triage, 24-hour remediation target for customer-impacting incidents; add optional premium 30-min response at extra cost
Throughput SLOs: include engineered throughput guarantees for reserved pool (e.g., 16 GPUs => sustained 220 req/s for 8k-token window); include perf test artifacts as acceptance criteria for go-live

Failover & residency: commit to cross-region failover plan within 15 minutes for control-plane route and 60s for data-plane reconnection where possible; note: full KV-cache warmup may affect cold-latency during failover — document expected RTO on playbook
